claims.text: The starting material is the (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy.
The unchanged alloy exhibits caloric behavior under applied magnetic and pressure fields.
The unchanged alloy has poor load-bearing integrity and a tendency to crack.
A tailored HIP treatment will produce a fine, uniformly distributed secondary phase in the target alloy.
The HIP-induced secondary phase will arrest crack propagation and increase load-bearing integrity.
The tailored HIP treatment can generate the secondary phase without altering the phase transformation responsible for the caloric effect.
The intended structural mediator is a nanometric secondary phase analogous to HCP phases observed after HIP in another high-entropy alloy.
Uniformly dispersed precipitates will reinforce grain boundaries.
Uniformly dispersed precipitates will impede crack initiation and propagation.
The high-temperature, high-pressure HIP environment followed by tuned cooling will enable a subtle eutectoid or precipitation reaction.
The resulting fine precipitates will enhance dislocation pinning.
The resulting fine precipitates will enhance grain-boundary cohesion.
The precipitate-mediated microstructure will improve toughness.
The precipitate-mediated microstructure will improve tensile strength.
The HIP-induced structural changes will not interfere with the magnetocaloric or barocaloric phase transitions.
HIP treatment will increase the target alloy's microhardness by approximately 20–50% relative to the untreated alloy.
HIP treatment will increase the target alloy's tensile strength by approximately 20–50% relative to the untreated alloy.
The HIP-treated alloy will retain a caloric-response magnitude similar to that of the untreated alloy under magnetic and pressure fields.
The HIP-treated alloy will retain an operational caloric temperature window similar to that of the untreated alloy.
Excessively high HIP temperatures or overly rapid cooling may alter the caloric transition.
